speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) from 2012 to date, what is the number of complaints received regarding job discrimination faced by people with disabilities; (b) whether the Ministry has received feedback from individuals or organisations on job discrimination faced by people with disabilities during this period; (c) what are the main examples of discrimination; and (d) whether the Ministry will study the need for an anti-discrimination law to protect such persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We expect all employers to abide by the principles of fair and merit-based employment practices outlined in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: All the four cases were closed after TAFEP provided advice to the employers to improve their employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We urge all individuals who feel that they have been discriminated against to approach TAFEP for advice and assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In fact, such laws may have the unintended consequence of deterring employers from hiring them in the first instance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This may happen when employers are fearful that workers cannot be dismissed even with legitimate reasons or that their actions would be misconstrued as being unlawful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The key to addressing discrimination is to change mindsets, and the effective tools for achieving this goes beyond legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, MOM supports employers through the Open Door Programme and Special Employment Credit scheme to improve employment outcomes for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: TAFEP also promotes fair and inclusive employment practices and contribute to better employment outcomes for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would just like to refer the Minister of State to the recent study conducted by the Disabled People's Association, together with the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) and the insights that they had discovered with regard to the unfair practices against people with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am wondering what the Ministry's position is on it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I note that the numbers are not big, but it does tell or show towards some discrimination which are not spoken of or where it is not clear whether there is discrimination, especially when no reasons are given when they are not given promotion or where they are not given the jobs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I am also wondering what the Ministry's position is on that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: And I appreciate the difficulties and the counter-effect of having legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But without legislation, it is very difficult to enforce or implement certain policies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am wondering if there is a middle ground on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We could impose certain requirements or policies where you would require some sort of transparency when we speak about promotion or in employing people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We take every discriminatory practice, whether for persons with disabilities or otherwise, very seriously.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, in fact, recently, the tripartite partners have also launched two tripartite standards that will help encourage companies not to have discriminatory practices, including against persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One was launched last November when we launched the Tripartite Standards of Recruitment Practices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The other one was in October when we launched the Tripartite Standards on Grievance Handling.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These efforts are complemented by more specific measures by MOM, SGEnable and voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) to help persons with disabilities gain employment and support employers to hire persons with disabilities through programmes, such as the Open-door Programme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, more importantly, the law today covers those who are disabled and those who are not under the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the Employment Act, individuals who feel that they are wrongfully dismissed, including due to the disability, may appeal to MOM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If substantiated, MOM will take action against the employer, including requiring the errant employer to compensate the individual.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We urge all individuals who feel that they have been wrongfully dismissed to approach MOM for advice and assistance as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On occasions, we have also heard of employers who have made special arrangements for their disabled employees.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MOM consider working with the Labour Movement and non-government organisations (NGOs), such as the Disabled People's Association, to raise awareness on the best practices by these enlightened employers with disabled employees?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To help address discrimination against persons with disabilities, the Government takes a holistic and comprehensive approach through the Third Enabling Master Plan (EMP3) and this is done in collaboration by MOM with the Ministry of Social and Family Development and SGEnable to maximise the potential and opportunities for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The EMP3 serves as a road map for Singapore to build a more inclusive society where persons with disabilities are empowered to contribute and realise their potential.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am also glad that the Member asked about the involvement of the tripartite partners because, as I alluded to Member Rahayu Mahzam's questions earlier, in addition to supporting EMP3, MOM launched two Tripartite Standards to Promote Inclusive Hiring Practices and Manage Workplace Grievances.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As part of the Tripartite Standard of Recruitment Practices, the Standard encourages fair, merit-based and inclusive hiring practices for persons with disabilities, among other groups.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Last October, when we launched the Tripartite Standard for Grievance Handling, the standard applied specifies a set of variable and actionable employment practices for companies to manage workplace grievances, including allegations of discrimination more effectively.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers adopting this standard commit to put in place clear processes for handling employees' grievances to ensure that these are adequately dealt with.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM's focus is now to encourage more employers to adopt this standard and we will certainly support our Tripartite Partners in this endeavour.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The short answer was yes and yes to both questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
